My instructor pilot, Geoff Morrell, in the left-hand seat, was one of four instructor pilots who would be with us in Shannon
A veteran flight engineer instructor, Arthur Winstanley, was in the flight engineer’s seat behind me
There were two types of instructors: the ‘soft cuddly kind’ (as we cadet pilots mistakenly thought of them), who included Morrell and Winstanley, and the more gruff, taciturn variety
The latter included Bob Knights, known affectionately as ‘Chopper’, who, right now, was sitting with the others in the back of the aircraft
As I taxied out, besides the practice I’d done on the sim, the only point of reference I had for steering an aircraft on the ground was driving a car
On a car, steering is intuitive – you turn the wheel, you touch the brakes, and the car does what you want it to
